3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I stood on the palace balcony, watching as a flurry of monarch butterflies drifted through the air, their orange wings catching the late spring afternoon sunlight.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: They had come from as far as Rumburg, journeying thousands of miles to reach southern Xina, where they would winter.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Rizia lay in the heart of their migration path.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: I had seen them before, but this time, something about their passage struck me differently.

7.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
7.text: Perhaps it was the timing – this season of change, of endings and beginnings.

8.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
8.text: I couldn't help but think that I, too, had traveled a great distance.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: I was not the man I had been when I first took the throne.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: A knock at the door drew me from my thoughts.

11.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
11.text: I thought about how the flutter of a butterfly's wings could send ripples through the air, unseen but far-reaching.

12.speaker: Player_Romus_Italic
12.text: I couldn't stop thinking about how when butterflies land on you, they’re tasting you with their feet.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: How even the smallest decisions in my reign -- those made in quiet moments -- could set off a chain of events far beyond my control.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: As their footsteps faded down the corridor, I turned my gaze to the window overlooking the garden.

19.speaker: Narrator
19.text: The sun had begun to set, and the silhouettes of butterflies fluttered against the fading light.

20.speaker: Narrator
20.text: I was once again reminded of the distance I had traveled to get here.

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: How my journey was far from over, and I would see it through to the end.

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: I was once again reminded that, like the seasons, I too had changed.

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: And my transformation would carry me far into the future.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: I was once again reminded of how the smallest of actions could result in consequences far beyond my control.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: I was once again reminded that they taste with their feet -- how life is fully of strange, unexpected oddities.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: And that as King of Rizia, it was my sole responsibility to deal with whatever came my way.

27.speaker: Narrator
27.text: And no matter how strange the journey ahead might be, I would face the future head-on.

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: With no Grand Vizier to mediate between me and the matters of my kingdom, I alone was responsible for reviewing them.

43.speaker: Narrator

47.speaker: Narrator

48.speaker: Narrator
